threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use your phone to navigate; everyone else just knows the secret backstreets and which way the bus actually goes.
Caught a guy holding a bouquet of flowers at 3 AM, chatting up the driver like they were old mates. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids using a bus stop as a skateboard ramp while an elderly man shook his head, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the U-Bahn stations here have the best graffiti? It’s like an art gallery underground, changing with the seasons.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's from here by how they navigate the BART delays—locals just roll their eyes and grab a burrito instead of complaining.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing the accordion on the Muni, totally out of tune but somehow lifted the whole mood. That’s the SF spirit, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think Gràcia is just another Gaudí spot—missing the true charm of its local artists and hidden squares buzzing with life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they stare at the metro map like it's a treasure map—glancing up at every stop like it's a surprise.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to call it 'London Fields Park.' Around here, it’s just 'the Fields'—everyone knows what you're talking about.
Caught a guy singing to his reflection in the bus window last night. Couldn't tell if he was serenading himself or just really into the late-night vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids playing soccer with an old trash can lid as a goal in the park, I thought, 'Yep, this is home.'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you’re in Kreuzberg when a street artist sets up an impromptu gallery with just spray paint and the whole block stops to admire the chaos.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name the exact corner where the old taco stand used to be before the fancy eateries took over.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters at Civic Center today while waiting for the bus. Totally nailed 'Stand By Me'—everyone forgot the delays, even if just for a moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the hidden squares where locals gather, like Plaça de la Virreina.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell when someone’s new: they’re still fumbling with the metro map while the locals glide past, earbuds in, ignoring it all.
